question: What is the main purpose of multi-sectorial collaboration during a disaster?

options.A: To allow different agencies to work as a unified front
options.B: To let the health ministry manage all rescue operations
options.C: To reduce the total number of volunteers needed
options.D: To ensure only government agencies handle relief funds

explanation: Disasters require many different groups to combine their strengths so they can respond effectively together. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why can no single agency handle a major disaster completely on its own?

options.A: Government rules forbid any agency from working alone
options.B: Agencies prefer to wait for outside help before starting
options.C: Individual organizations lack any trained leadership staff
options.D: No single agency has all the necessary resources and expertise

explanation: Major emergencies overwhelm the capacity of any single group, making teamwork across various sectors necessary for survival and recovery. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: What does the principle of Unity of Command mean in disaster response?

options.A: All agencies must share the exact same financial budget
options.B: Every team member writes their own daily work schedule
options.C: The head of state makes all tactical field decisions
options.D: Every responder answers to only one designated supervisor

explanation: Unity of command stops confusion by making sure every worker reports to a single clear boss. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h2)

question: Why is standardized terminology important when different agencies respond together?

options.A: It forces foreign donors to learn the local dialect quickly
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings caused by agency jargon
options.C: It replaces the need for any written communication logs
options.D: It ensures that reports can only be read by senior directors

explanation: When everyone uses the same clear words for equipment and roles, costly mistakes and delays are avoided. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which sector is primarily responsible for crowd control and maintaining safety during a disaster?
explanation: Police and military forces handle public safety, traffic flow, and security in disaster zones. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h3)

question: A nurse needs to find temporary clean drinking water and sanitation tents for displaced villagers. Which sector should the nurse contact first?
explanation: The Shelter and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene sector handles safe housing and clean water supplies for affected populations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why do nurses act as crucial links between affected communities and coordinators?

options.A: They hold the highest administrative rank in disaster management
options.B: They interact directly with victims and understand ground realities
options.C: They are the only health professionals allowed outside hospitals
options.D: They control the transport and logistics budgets for the region

explanation: Because nurses care directly for the victims, they see what resources are missing and report those needs to coordinators. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common duty for nurses in a multi-sectorial disaster team?

options.A: Negotiating international trade agreements for relief goods
options.B: Directing military troop movements in the field zone
options.C: Issuing building permits for temporary shelters
options.D: Triaging mass casualties and managing field clinics

explanation: Nurses use their clinical training to sort injured patients and run emergency treatment stations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why is it necessary to use redundant communication systems during a disaster response?

options.A: Radio frequencies are too expensive for humanitarian groups
options.B: Paper notes are too heavy to carry around a disaster zone
options.C: Different agencies are legally banned from using mobile phones
options.D: Standard cellular networks and internet lines frequently collapse

explanation: Disasters routinely destroy power grids and cell towers, so teams need backup tools like satellite radios and runners. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is a major risk when communication channels break down during an emergency?

options.A: All patients instantly recover without needing professional care
options.B: Rescuers automatically receive extra funding from international donors
options.C: Rumors spread and leaders make poor decisions based on bad data
options.D: Hospitals stop admitting any new patients until power returns

explanation: Without reliable information, panic grows and coordinators cannot direct help to where it is truly needed. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal of inventory tracking in disaster supply warehouses?

options.A: To ensure all medical equipment is painted the same color
options.B: To prove to tax authorities that the agency made a profit
options.C: To calculate the exact salaries of international volunteers
options.D: To prevent stockouts and stop expired medications from going out

explanation: Good inventory tracking ensures health teams always have safe, working supplies available for patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective cross-sector collaboration?

options.A: Competing institutional egos and reluctance to share credit
options.B: Instant agreement and seamless sharing of all financial budgets
options.C: Cultural differences between military and humanitarian groups
options.D: Bureaucratic red tape and slow administrative approval processes

explanation: Agencies rarely reach instant financial agreement; instead, funding disputes and mistrust are common barriers that teams must overcome. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h7)

question: Why do different organizational cultures, such as military versus humanitarian groups, cause friction in a response?

options.A: They operate under conflicting leadership styles and operational rules
options.B: Humanitarian workers refuse to wear protective boots
options.C: They are legally forbidden from speaking to one another in public
options.D: They always use completely different spoken languages

explanation: Rigid military hierarchies and flexible volunteer groups often clash over how decisions should be made in the field. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of an after-action review (AAR) following a disaster?

options.A: To evaluate successes and failures so future responses can improve
options.B: To calculate the final financial profits of private contractors
options.C: To rewrite the national constitution for emergency powers
options.D: To punish staff members who made minor administrative errors

explanation: Debriefing after an event helps teams learn valuable lessons and fix coordination mistakes for the next emergency. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h8)

question: Why are joint multi-agency simulation drills important before a disaster happens?

options.A: They allow international donors to inspect local hospital buildings
options.B: They build personal trust and working familiarity among different responders
options.C: They eliminate the need for any written emergency response plans
options.D: They guarantee that natural disasters will completely bypass the region

explanation: Training together beforehand ensures that different agencies know each other's styles and work smoothly together when lives are on the line. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h8)
